You are a strategic thinker with strong technical depth, passionate about designing robust architectures for complex systems. You thrive in collaborative environments and enjoy influencing both technical and standardization directions.

- Ensure compliance with 3GPP standards while optimizing for satellite-specific constraints
- Collaborate with system engineers, protocol experts, and hardware teams to deliver integrated solutions
- Evaluate emerging technologies and propose architectural improvements
- Contribute to internal design reviews and development efforts

Must have

- Proven experience in software architecture for wireless communication systems
- Strong software engineering skills and experience with distributed systems
- Ability to translate complex requirements into scalable architectural designs
- Excellent communication skills

Nice to have

- Experience with 5G NTN concepts and satellite communications
- Understanding of 3GPP 5G NR specifications, especially RAN architecture
- Experience in 5G RAN stack development
- Background in embedded systems or performance-critical networking software

Role overview

Reporting to the VP, Corporate Finance & Strategy, you work directly on the company’s most significant transactions: acquisitions and investments, equity financing, strategic partnerships and investor relations. The team is small and the mandates are large and live, so you own substantive parts of real deals early rather than support from a distance. In a given week you might move between a strategic mapping of the industry, a due-diligence stream, a board memo and an investor data room.

The seat offers unusual range for one role (M&A, capital raising, corporate development, strategy and investor relations under a single mandate) with direct exposure to the executive team and the company’s investors, and a growing volume of deals and financings as the company scales. You take ownership and responsibility early.

The position is full-time and permanent, based in Belgium (Mont-Saint-Guibert / Charleroi) with hybrid working and some international travel. Compensation is a competitive base plus equity participation in the business.

Key activities

M&A and strategic transactions

- · Build and maintain business plans and transaction models: three-statement operating models, DCF and sum-of-the-parts valuations, returns and sensitivities.
- · Support execution from origination and screening through due diligence, structuring, negotiation and integration planning across acquisitions, joint ventures, minority investments and partnerships.
- · Coordinate diligence workstreams and manage external advisors: banks, legal, tax, technical and financial.
- · Write the board and investment-committee papers: the analysis, the options, the recommendation.
- · Support the shareholder-agreement, governance and capital-structure work tied to deals and financings.

Financing and capital markets

- Support equity rounds and other capital raises: equity story, investor materials, capitalisation table and dilution analysis, and term-sheet review.
- Build and run the investor pipeline and CRM; profile and prioritise targets across sovereign wealth funds, growth-equity firms, strategics and family offices.
- Prepare and run the data room and handle investor diligence requests.
- Contribute to public-markets work.
- Strategy and market intelligence
- Produce competitive and sector analysis across space, defence and deep tech: comparables, financing and M&A activity, market sizing, value-chain mapping.
- Build the business cases for new markets, programmes and capabilities.
- Turn commercial, technical and geopolitical inputs into the analysis leadership uses to decide.

Investor relations

- Prepare investor reporting and shareholder updates.
- Help manage relationships with existing investors and lenders.

Must have

- 3–7 years in investment banking (M&A, leveraged finance, ECM or coverage), private equity, growth equity, transaction services or strategy consulting.
- The ability to build, not just run, a three-statement model, a DCF and an LBO from scratch.
- Rigour and accuracy: your numbers are right and your reasoning is clear.
- Clear, concise writing and clean Excel and PowerPoint; materials a board or an investor can act on directly.
- The ability to carry several live deadlines at once and prioritise well under pressure.
- Discretion and judgement with confidential information.
- An interest in European technological and industrial sovereignty.
- Fluent English; working French strongly preferred and useful day-to-day in Belgium.
- Eligibility to work in Belgium / the EU.

Nice to have

- An engineering or technical degree; we want someone who can understand the products and the industry, not only the financials.
- Hands-on experience in aerospace, defence, space, hardware or another capital-intensive, technically complex industry.
- Cross-border M&A and public-markets experience (IPO, P2P, PIPE).

Shortlisted candidates complete a financial-modelling and strategic-case exercise as part of the interview process.

- Understanding of the full EP subsystem chain: thruster, PPU, propellant storage and feed system, and associated control and telemetry.
- Experience managing technical interfaces with suppliers or partners, including specifications, ICDs, and progress follow-up.

Your mission is to build a robust, qualified, and scalable supply chain for printed circuit boards across all satellite programmes, enabling Aerospacelab’s constellation expansion ambitions.

You will perform a company-wide analysis of all PCBs to be manufactured, derive the annual production volumes, and determine the number and profile of suppliers required. PCB Demand Analysis & Panel Strategy

- Conduct a company-wide inventory of all PCBs across all satellite programmes, consolidating BOMs and design data into a structured demand baseline.
- Derive annual PCB production volumes per board type and translate them into supplier capacity and panel sizing requirements.
- Define the target supplier panel architecture: number of suppliers, geographic spread, technology coverage, and dual-source strategy (baseline + alternative per PCB type).

Supplier qualification is the central and most critical activity of this role. For each PCB type, you will lead the full qualification process from identification to production release:

- Identify and evaluate new EMS and PCB suppliers through RFI/RFQ processes, technical audits, and manufacturing capability assessments.
- Lead New Product Introduction (NPI) phases: coordinate Design, Quality, Industrialization, and Procurement stakeholders at both ASL and supplier side to ensure smooth qualification campaigns.

- EEE Component experts, to align component choices with PCB manufacturability and supplier constraints.

Your mission

You translate mission and customer requirements into reliability and safety budgets, drive the supporting analyses (FMECA, FTA, reliability predictions, FDIR adequacy), and act as the technical authority on dependability across the satellite bus, payload, and ground/operations interfaces. You work hand-in-hand with systems, AOCS, EPS, avionics, software, and Product Assurance teams, and represent the RAMS discipline at programme milestones and customer reviews.

Key responsibilities

- Define, allocate, and track reliability, availability, and safety budgets at system, subsystem, and equipment level, including apportionment to suppliers.
- Plan and conduct FMEA / FMECA analyses (functional and hardware), identify single points of failure, and maintain the Critical Items List (CIL) and associated mitigation/retention rationale.
- Perform and review reliability predictions (parts-count and parts-stress) using ECSS-Q-ST-30 series, MIL-HDBK-217 or FIDES, and consolidate Reliability Block Diagrams (RBD) and Fault Tree Analyses (FTA).
- Assess constellation-level availability (mean number of operational satellites, service continuity, replenishment strategy) and feed results back into the system and operations design.
- Evaluate the adequacy of FDIR (Failure Detection, Isolation and Recovery) and autonomy concepts against identified failure modes.

About Aerospacelab

As we continue to expand our team, we are seeking a talented and motivated Satellite Cybersecurity Architect to make sure the software we fly is secure by design and that our satellites cannot be compromised.

As Satellite Cybersecurity Architect, you will define and own the cybersecurity architecture across our satellite platforms: setting the secure development practices our software teams follow, designing and implementing mechanisms such as secure boot, and owning the strategy for how cryptographic keys are generated, distributed, stored, and rotated across the fleet. You will work closely with the Satellite Software Architect, Embedded Software Engineers, and EE/FPGA engineers to embed security into the architecture from the start rather than bolting it on afterwards, and with satellite operators and V&V teams to make sure security requirements are actually verified and hold up in operations.

At Aerospacelab, our motto is work hard, play hard. We strive to innovate, in a fun and inclusive work environment. We work in short cycles — no waiting for years before seeing designs go live and get valuable feedback. Expect an exciting job, where you will learn constantly and help make sure that what we build stays trustworthy once it's in orbit.

Key Activities

- Define and own the satellite cybersecurity architecture, covering on-board software, unit-level firmware, and the interfaces between units.
- Establish secure coding standards and development best practices (e.g. secure SDLC, code review guidelines, static/dynamic analysis) and support software teams in applying them.
- Design and implement secure boot and trusted execution methodologies and flows across our on-board computers and units.
- Define and own the strategy and processes for cryptographic key management: generation, distribution, storage, rotation, and revocation across satellite platforms and missions.
- Perform threat modeling and security risk assessments on satellite software and communication links (TT&C, payload data links), and define mitigations.
- Define security requirements at satellite and unit level, and ensure they are traceable and verified through the V&V process.
- Collaborate with the Satellite Software Architect, Embedded Software Engineers, and FPGA/EE engineers to embed security into architectural and design decisions from the start.
- Coordinate with satellite operators and ground-segment IT security teams to make sure security is maintained consistently from on-board software to ground infrastructure.
- Stay current on emerging space cybersecurity threats and standards, and continuously improve Aerospacelab's security posture based on lessons learnt.

Must Have

- MSc, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field.
- Solid experience in embedded systems security, with hands-on knowledge of C and Python.
- Practical experience with secure boot, trusted execution, or hardware root-of-trust concepts.
- Solid understanding of cryptography fundamentals and key management practices (symmetric/asymmetric encryption, key exchange, PKI).
- Ability to lead technical discussions, structure trade-offs clearly, and communicate security decisions to multidisciplinary teams that may not have a security background.

- Demonstrated ability to work across teams to drive security practices to adoption with a high degree of autonomy.

Role overview

As a Unit Thermomechanical Engineer, you will be responsible for the design, analysis, validation, and production of satellite units, whatever their underlying technology. Around each unit's core, you will design the mechanical structure so it withstands the thermal, structural, and radiation environments it will face throughout the mission.You will own these aspects end-to-end for your assigned units: 3D design and production drawings, radiation, thermal, and structural design, as well as environmental tests (vibration and thermal). You'll work hands-on across the full lifecycle, from early design through validation and production.This is a great opportunity to build broad, hands-on technical expertise across four demanding engineering domains, mechanical, thermal, structural, and radiation, while progressively growing into a role with real ownership and autonomy over flight hardware.

Key responsibilities

- Design the mechanical structure of satellite units, from concept to detailed design, adapted to each unit's specific technology (electronic, electromechanical, etc.).
- Produce 3D models and manufacturing drawings for unit parts.
- Perform thermal analysis and tests to ensure units operate within their components' thermal limits.
- Perform structural analysis and vibration testing campaigns to ensure the unit and its components withstand vibration loads.
- Perform radiation analysis (TID/TNID) and spot shield sensitive electronic components if needed.
- Support validation testing and troubleshooting, working closely with the EEE team and suppliers.
- Progressively take ownership of units with increasing autonomy, with guidance from senior engineers in the guild.

Must have

- 1 to 4 years of experience in aerospace or another relevant mechanical, thermal, or structural engineering field, with exposure to CAD design, structural and/or thermal modelling.
- Good foundations in mechanical design and manufacturing drawings, as well as modelling and testing.
- Interest in developing broad, cross-disciplinary expertise (mechanical, thermal, structural, radiation).
- Excellent communication skills.
- Fast learner, result-oriented.
- Fluency in English.
- Willingness to challenge the European space industry status quo.

Nice to have

- Exposure to FEA tools (structural or thermal).
- Experience with vibration and/or thermal testing.
- Familiarity with radiation effects on electronics (TID/TNID).
- Experience in space or satellite-related projects (academic or professional).
